bugs.what: Using the hunter's-camp secret gap to open the Vale barrow doors made the priest's 'blessing' quest option retroactively moot ('the doors are already open') with no warning beforehand, closing off a piece of dialogue content.
bugs.where: Barrow Field / Gray Chapel, Act I

bugs.what: Keeper Wren's 'Two Keepers, One Covenant' quest (find Rowan in Thornwold's Understory) became uncompletable after I settled Thornwold's grief by reading the hanged names instead of visiting Rowan, but the quest log still lists it as open/pending rather than marking it closed.

Numbered menu options sometimes shift by one between an action and its immediate follow-up screen (e.g. 'speak with the company' moved from slot 6 to 5 after a quest completed), causing an accidental wrong selection once.

confusions: Room-to-room compass directions in wilderness areas (Iron Downs downs, Wardmoor moor) were not always geometrically consistent — 'south' from one node sometimes led back the way I'd come rather than continuing a logical loop, making backtracking via cardinal directions unreliable; 'get your bearings' was needed constantly to reorient.

It's not obvious up front that recruiting all four companions simultaneously is possible and encouraged — the game doesn't say so until you've already recruited a couple and it surfaces as a passive note.

The threshold for what counts toward 'hollows rested' (bargains count, burns don't) versus the separate 'Old Court Evidence'/'Crypts laid to rest' sub-trackers wasn't clear until reading status closely; a first-time player could easily under- or over-invest in side content.
suggestions: Surface the 'you can recruit every companion, not just one' hint at the very first recruitment offer, not after the fact.

When an action (like using a secret entrance) silently invalidates a later dialogue option, have the NPC or scene text flag that the standard path is now closed before the player commits to the shortcut.
Add a lightweight compass/map recap option in wilderness zones specifically, since node-to-node direction naming was the least consistent part of an otherwise very well-signposted game.

The 'name it (stands down)' peaceful-resolution option for guardian enemies is excellent design (barrow-wight, gray sergeant, honour guard, etc.) — consider surfacing it as a discoverable mechanic earlier/more explicitly, since I found it by trial rather than being told it existed.
